payload.excerpt: that happily accepts a current version. The hand-pin in requirements.txt is the only thing holding aiohttp at 3.10.10. Removing the pin and letting the resolver take ≥3.14.3 resolves all of them in one move. aiohttp is not imported anywhere in this codebase (grep confirms) — it's purely transitive, and pinning transitive dependencies by hand is what created the exposure. Also: Black carries a HIGH CVE and is a runtime dependency OSV returns 3 advisories for black==24.10.0: - CVE-2026-32274 — HIGH, arbitrary file writes from unsanitized input in the cache filename. Affects >=24.3.0 - CVE-2026-31900 (PYSEC-2026-2120) Ordinarily a formatter's CVEs are a shrug. These matter because Black is pinned as a runtime dependency, so it ships into the production image. Moving it to a dev group resolves both. Verification Queried https://api.osv.dev/v1/query for each package at its pinned version. Counts and IDs above are from that res
